article.articleHeadline: Rajasthan: 2 die of Chandipura virus, state steps up surveillance
article.articleSummary: Chandipura virus (CHPV) deaths in Rajasthan and Gujarat prompt heightened surveillance in Dungarpur, Sirohi, and Udaipur districts. A six-year-old from Dungarpur’s Ratanpura died at Civil Hospital, Himmatnagar (Sabarkantha), and a two-year-old from Sirohi died in a hospital in Banaskantha, Gujarat. By July 24, nine CHPV deaths have been confirmed in the current outbreak—seven in Gujarat and two in Rajasthan. CHPV, transmitted by infected sandfly bites, belongs to the Rhabdoviridae family and can cause encephalitis. Children under 15 are most vulnerable; symptoms include high fever, vomiting, seizures, and altered consciousness, with rapid progression. Cases tend to appear during the monsoon season. The virus was first identified in 1965 in Chandipura village, Maharashtra. The six-year-old fell ill July 12 and died July 15 after tests confirmed CHPV; authorities surveyed 75 households in Ratanpura, reporting no suspected cases and launched fogging and awareness efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Eerste proefpersoon krijgt vaccin tegen Bundibugyo-variant ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: First volunteer receives vaccine against Bundibugyo Ebola variant.
article.articleSummary: First volunteer in Oxford, England, has been vaccinated with an experimental vaccine against the Bundibugyo variant of Ebola. The Phase I trial at Oxford enrolls 50 healthy adults aged 18–55 to assess safety; participants will not be exposed to the virus, but antibody responses will indicate potential protection. The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak is ongoing in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with neighboring Uganda affected; since late April, roughly 2,500 cases have been reported and over 1,000 deaths. If safe and immunogenic, the vaccine could be deployed promptly, with 600,000 doses already produced in anticipation of approval. Later, the vaccine will also be given to people in Congo. Two other vaccines are in development, with Oxford's being the first to reach human testing.

triage.notes: 記事本文はオックスフォードでのワクチン治験に関するものだが、背景として言及されているコンゴ民主共和国での大規模エボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）流行が主要な公衆衛生上の懸念事項である。ウガンダも影響を受けているが対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。英国（オックスフォード）は治験実施地であり発生地ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: 非洲埃博拉疫情死亡人数破千：疫区人道、安全危机交织
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Africa's Ebola outbreak death toll tops 1,000 as humanitarian and security crises intertwine in affected areas.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo (Ituri and North Kivu, Bunia) and Uganda has killed over 1,000 people. As of July 20, DRC reported 2,473 confirmed cases and 999 deaths; Uganda had 20 cases and 2 deaths. World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus calls it the third-largest Ebola outbreak on record, with transmission accelerating in the past month. More than 80% of new infections are not linked to known contacts, indicating many undetected transmission chains. At least 16 displacement camps in Ituri host over 270,000 people, with crowded conditions and strained water, sanitation, and health services increasing spread risk. DRC has 23 treatment centers, 19 laboratories, and about 800 beds, but security issues and mistrust hinder response. Bundibugyo Ebola has no licensed vaccine; vaccine/therapeutic candidates are in trials. Uganda’s last patient was discharged on July 16; a 42-day observation will decide if the outbreak ends.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカのエボラ出血熱、死者数1,000人突破：被災地で人道・治安危機が複合
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3項目該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大）に加え、WPRO基準も全項目該当し、WHO事務局長も言及するなど社会的関心が極めて高い大規模アウトブレイクである。
triage.notes: ウガンダでも症例が報告されているが、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。DRC（イトゥリ州・ブニア）が主な発生地であり、感染連鎖の80%以上が既知接触者と関連しないなど、地域拡大・見逃し感染のリスクが高い。ワクチン未承認、治安不安による対応困難も懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola deaths pass 1,000 in the DRC, faster than any previous outbreak
article.articleSummary: Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpassed 1,000 deaths 67 days after declaration on May 15, 2026. As of July 21, 2026, 2,536 confirmed cases, 1,033 deaths and 506 recoveries; 63 new cases and 34 new deaths; 306 suspected, 738 in isolation. Transmission remains active in Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo. Uganda reports 20 cases and 2 deaths; one case in France, totaling 2,557 confirmed cases and 1,035 deaths. Ituri accounts for about 90% of cases and over 80% of deaths. No licensed vaccine or treatment exists; surveillance is limited (82% of identified contacts traced; WHO target 90–95%; Africa CDC notes fewer than 9% monitored). In late June, an Ebola treatment centre in Ituri was attacked and set on fire, killing two people. A Bundibugyo clade with 219 SNPs; Oxford began Phase I Bundibugyo vaccine trial on July 13; Ervebo guidance remains cautious.

article.articleHeadline: Costa Rica recibe cooperación de Panamá, Brasil y Perú contra la leishmaniasis
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Costa Rica receives cooperation from Panama, Brazil and Peru to combat leishmaniasis.
article.articleSummary: Costa Rica receives 6,800 units of leishmaniasis treatment donated by Panama, Brazil, and Peru to address drug shortages as the country reports 369 cases in 2026. Leishmaniasis is a cutaneous disease caused by Leishmania and transmitted by female Lutzomyia sandflies, popularly known as papalomoyo. The Ministry of Health notes the donations strengthen national capacity to ensure timely access to essential medicines for diagnosed patients. The Costa Rican Social Security Fund (CCSS) will perform the technical review and manage logistics for distribution. Preventive measures include cleaning surroundings, proper waste disposal, installing screens on doors/windows, using insect repellent, wearing clothing that covers most of the body in forested areas, and responsible pet ownership with regular veterinary checks. The cooperation highlights international alliances to safeguard public health amid shortages.

article.articleHeadline: إفيروس يخرج عن السيطرة في الكونغو.. انتشار غير مسبوق يثير القلق
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A virus spiraling out of control in the Democratic Republic of the Congo... unprecedented spread raises concerns.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo is escalating, with 2,536 confirmed cases and 1,033 deaths reported; about 738 patients are in treatment centers. The outbreak centers in Ituri Province, including Kisangani, and into Uganda. The active strain is Bundibugyo, for which there are no licensed vaccines or approved therapies. Health authorities say transmission continues, though recent fluctuations may reflect reporting delays and data consolidation. WHO classifies risk as very high in DRC and high in Uganda and neighboring countries, while global risk remains low because transmission occurs by direct contact, not airborne. MSF notes the initial scale was unprecedented; delayed detection allowed wider spread. CDC modeling warns the outbreak could approach the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. Response challenges include armed conflict in eastern DRC, displacement, rumors and distrust, health worker strikes over delayed salaries, and that only 77% of known contacts are being followed—far below 95%.

article.articleHeadline: Cegah TB Jadi Aktif dengan Terapi Pencegahan untuk Kontak Erat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Prevent TB from Becoming Active with Preventive Therapy for Close Contacts
article.articleSummary: As of 25 July 2026, Indonesia's Ministry of Health is expanding TB control with the Free Health Check program (CKG), including chest X-ray screening at 53,335 sites nationwide to detect TB early and protect high-risk contacts. Those diagnosed with TB will receive treatment promptly, while asymptomatic close contacts will be offered Tuberculosis Preventive Therapy (TPT) to prevent latent infection from progressing. Officials stress cross-sector collaboration and community engagement, noting that sustained X-ray access and public awareness are key to eliminating TB. In East Java's Jember Regency, the government launched a Homecare program titled 'Realizing a Family Doctor for the Underprivileged,' enabling health workers to conduct home visits for basic checks, education, and telemedicine consultations when needed. The combined national-local approach aims to close household transmission gaps and accelerate TB elimination in Indonesia.

article.articleHeadline: BKHIT Maluku perketat pengawasan lalu lintas unggas cegah flu burung
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Maluku's BKHIT tightens oversight of poultry movement to prevent avian influenza.
article.articleSummary: Avian Influenza prevention measures in Maluku: The Balai Karantina Hewan, Ikan, dan Tumbuhan (BKHIT) Maluku tightens oversight of poultry movement at ports and airports to prevent Avian Influenza (AI) entry into Maluku. In Ambon, BKHIT rejected entry of live chickens without quarantine documents on KM Permata Obi via Yos Sudarso Port, as part of animal quarantine to avert Hama Penyakit Hewan Karantina (HPHK). Any live chicken imports must have a Health Certificate (SKH), quarantine documents from the origin, and be reported to quarantine officers for inspection. Birds must undergo physical health checks to ensure they are free from contagious animal diseases, including AI. The restrictions apply regardless of the number of animals. Authorities will strengthen checks at all entry points under Law No. 21 of 2019 on Animal, Fish, and Plant Quarantine. Public and business operators should ensure all quarantine requirements before inter-regional movement of animals to prevent spread.

article.articleHeadline: Kasus Terus Meningkat, Ini Pentingnya Mencegah Penyakit TBC dengan Tips Berikut
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cases Continue to Rise: The Importance of Preventing Tuberculosis with the Following Tips.
article.articleSummary: Over one million new tuberculosis (TB) cases occur annually in Indonesia, the country with the highest TB burden, affecting all ages. Mycobacterium tuberculosis transmission is driven by close contact with infected individuals and aerosolized droplets, particularly where ventilation is poor. Preventive measures emphasized include: avoiding close contact with coughing or sneezing TB patients; not sharing personal items; wearing masks in crowded or poorly ventilated public spaces; regular hand hygiene; maintaining robust immune health via nutritious diets, regular exercise, and adequate rest; and obtaining the BCG vaccine, routinely given to babies before age two, with adults who have not been vaccinated encouraged to get it. The article underscores collective responsibility to curb spread and reduce incidence in Indonesia, citing the nationwide focus on TB prevention.

article.articleHeadline: Bé gái sốc nhiễm trùng, viêm phổi do phế cầu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Little girl with septic shock and pneumococcal pneumonia.
article.articleSummary: An 11-year-old girl, Phuong Chau, from An Giang Province, Vietnam, developed fever and cough that progressed to severe pneumococcal pneumonia with septic shock and sepsis-related cardiac injury. She required prolonged ICU care: mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, blood and platelet transfusions, continuous renal replacement therapy, and four weeks on ECMO to support heart and lungs. After two weeks, cardiac function gradually recovered, but she developed left-leg hypoperfusion with thrombosis of the vertebral and external iliac arteries, treated by thrombectomy and anticoagulation. Four CRRT sessions and about a month of ECMO were needed, with total costs near one billion đồng. Pneumococcus colonizes the nasopharynx and can invade when immunity is low, causing pneumonia, meningitis, sepsis, or other invasive disease. Vietnam offers pneumococcal vaccines (13, 15, 20, 23) for different ages; vaccination reduces disease and carriage and may yield substantial healthcare savings, per Lancet 2019. Parents are urged to seek early care for warning signs.

article.articleHeadline: Shopian still wakes up to pandemic messages
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 continues to be echoed in Shopian, as the Municipal Council Shopian (MCS) broadcasts COVID-19 safety advisories daily via loudspeakers mounted on garbage-collection vehicles. Each morning the vehicles travel residential areas and play reminders to maintain physical distancing, wear masks, and follow COVID-19 appropriate behaviour—messages dating from the pandemic’s peak. The World Health Organization had declared in May 2023 that COVID-19 no longer constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Residents say the loud announcements, at high volume, are intrusive and unnecessary now, especially for elderly residents, students, and those working from home. Some say only essential waste-management notices or sanitation messages should be broadcast. Others report interruptions to online meetings. Officials could not be reached for comment on whether the system will be updated or replaced.

article.articleHeadline: Cegah TB Berkembang Jadi Aktif dengan Terapi Pencegahan untuk Kontak Erat Pasien
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Prevent TB from progressing to active tuberculosis with preventive therapy for close contacts of patients
article.articleSummary: Indonesia’s Ministry of Health is accelerating TB elimination through the Free Health Check (CKG) program, deploying chest X-ray screenings at tens of thousands of sites to detect cases early and interrupt transmission. Deputy Health Minister Benjamin P. Octavianus says the strategy treats the sick and protects those at risk: diagnosed TB patients are treated promptly, while close contacts without symptoms receive Tuberculosis Preventive Therapy (TPT). TB bacteria can remain latent for 1–2 years, so early preventive therapy can prevent disease and curb spread. BP Taskin supports broader health access as a poverty-reduction investment. In Jember, East Java, the district launches Homecare program “Mewujudkan Dokter Keluarga untuk Masyarakat Tidak Mampu” to accelerate case finding via home visits, basic exams, education, and telemedicine, hoping the CKG chest X-ray and Jember model improve detection among close contacts.

article.articleHeadline: 瑞普生物制成我国首个全禽源重组禽流感灭活疫苗 津企为动物疫病防控贡献"中国方案"-新闻中心-北方网
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ruipu Biotech has developed China's first fully avian-origin recombinant avian influenza inactivated vaccine; Tianjin enterprises contribute to animal disease prevention and control with the 'China Solution' - News Center - Beifang Net.
article.articleSummary: Ruipu Biotech (Tianjin) and its subsidiary Huannan Biol. jointly led the project 'Vaccine Creation and Source Control for Avian Influenza: Key Technologies and Applications,' which won the National Science and Technology Progress Award (Second Prize). The initiative delivered China’s first fully avian-origin recombinant avian influenza inactivated vaccine and the world’s first waterfowl-specific H5 inactivated vaccine, plus a reverse-genetics vaccine platform for all-avian-origin influenza viruses. Targeting high-pathogenic H5 and H7 strains while addressing low-pathogenic H9, the program integrates 'vaccine + diagnostics' into a cohesive prevention framework. Multiple H5/H7 recombinant vaccines have obtained national new veterinary drug certificates and entered mandatory immunization catalogs, with nationwide coverage across core poultry regions and major farming enterprises. Diagnostics, guidelines, and surveillance tools are scaled nationally, and the China Solution has been exported to Belt and Road countries. Future plans emphasize industrialization, process optimization, and broader animal disease prevention applications.

article.articleHeadline: Au Kenya, le projet de centre de quarantaine pour ressortissants américains exposés à Ebola reste suspendu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Kenya, the proposed quarantine center for American citizens exposed to Ebola remains suspended.
article.articleSummary: July 25, 2026, Kenya's plan to open a quarantine center for American Ebola-exposed nationals at Laikipia Air Base remains suspended amid a legal challenge. The High Court of Nairobi heard July 23–24 arguments from plaintiffs who argued the project proceeded without consultation and risked public safety, claiming Kenya is not equipped to handle Ebola. Authorities insist the initiative is a preventive measure carried out in accordance with the law. A ruling is expected November 26, with the suspension preventing operationalization of the Laikipia facility. Separately, seven members of an American NGO are in quarantine on Kenyan soil after contributing to the Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Washington has confirmed transferring several American nationals to a center managed by American staff in Kenya with Nairobi's authorization, though the center's exact location remains undisclosed. The Katiba Institute condemns the actions; the Health Minister says compliance with the court.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Livestock explains the real cause of a mass die-off of sheep in central Sudan - Sudan News
article.articleSummary: In central Sudan’s Al Jazira state, the Batana area experienced reports of sheep die-offs, but the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries says these reports were inaccurate. The incident was limited and controlled more than a month ago. The ministry identified phosphorus deficiency in the local cattle feed as the cause, ruling out rinderpest/hemorrhagic septicemia, other viral diseases, or general feed shortage. Rapid intervention included distribution of feed cubes fortified with phosphorus and calcium, which helped contain the issue and halted fatalities. Officials described the deaths as limited and now fully stopped, and dismissed circulating rumors of a widespread outbreak as unfounded. The event reportedly occurred over a month prior and was addressed at that time. Keywords: phosphorus deficiency, Central Sudan, Al Jazira state, Batana area, sheep die-off, public health response.

triage.headline_ja: 畜産省、スーダン中部での羊の大量死の真の原因を説明

triage.notes: 対象国リストにスーダンは含まれず、また記事はフィリピン（Bluedotの発生地域に含まれる）とは無関係。牛疫は明確に否定されており、感染症イベントではないため対象国該当なし。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pimpri News: Eleven people contracted dengue; typhoid affecting 27,000 patients.
article.articleSummary: In Pimpri-Chinchwad (Pimpri) during monsoon 2026, dengue cases surged: two cases in June and 11 dengue cases in July, with 389 dengue-like cases in July and 11 confirmed as dengue. January–May saw no dengue; total dengue activity year-to-date is increasing. Typhoid fever (hivatap) surged with 27,072 cases reported in July. Malaria shows minimal activity, with one case each in June and July, bringing January–July total to 15. The authorities attribute expansion to water stagnation during the rains, fostering vector-borne transmission (dengue, chikungunya, malaria). Public health officials, including Dr. Laxman Gofane, state the dengue situation is under control but call for vigilance, hygiene, and prompt testing at municipal hospitals for fever and associated symptoms. Noted localized waterlogging reported in Koregaon and Nalavdewadi areas.

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola cases amount to 2,905 as vaccine enters human trial
article.articleSummary: DRC reports 2,905 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,269 deaths; 519 recovered and 722 in isolation or treatment. The rise stems from integrating Ituri and North Kivu data into the tally, not only new 24-hour reports. On Wednesday, 97 confirmed cases and 62 deaths were recorded. Kisangani, capital of the Tshopo province, reports patients arriving with severe symptoms; authorities will boost community training and awareness to encourage earlier care. The government allocated $50 million to the Ebola response, prioritizing laboratories, equipment, surveillance, and patient care. Oxford University announced the first volunteer vaccinated in the world's first human trial of a vaccine against Bundibugyo ebolavirus. The candidate, ChAdOx1 BDBV, by Oxford Vaccine Group and Pandemic Sciences Institute; Serum Institute of India has manufactured about 620,000 doses, including 4,000 investigational doses. Phase I will enroll 50 adults to assess safety and immune responses; if approved, further studies are planned in Uganda with partners.

article.articleHeadline: Thailand DDC Issues Warning as Rainy Season Bacterial Infections Claim Over 100 Lives
article.articleSummary: Thailand's Department of Disease Control (DDC) issued an urgent public health warning as rainy-season bacterial infections rise, with leptospirosis and melioidosis deaths surpassing 100 this year. From 1 January to 21 July 2026, leptospirosis recorded 2,190 cases and 30 deaths (case fatality rate 1.37%). Melioidosis tallied 1,654 cases and 77 deaths (CFR 4.66%), collectively driving over 100 fatalities. Highest infection rates are in the Southern and Northeastern regions; farmers, elderly residents, and people with frequent soil or standing-water contact are at greatest risk. Health officials advise wearing protective gear such as rubber boots, avoiding wading in floodwaters, and seeking prompt medical care for fever or muscle pain after potential exposure. Surveillance data from the Division of Epidemiology underpins the counts.

triage.notes: レプトスピラ症・類鼻疽は環境（土壌・水）由来の感染症で毎年雨季に発生する既知の季節性疾患。ヒト-ヒト感染はなく、国際的な公衆衛生上の脅威としての緊急性は低いが、死亡者数・CFRの高さから国内公衆衛生上の重要性はある。

article.articleHeadline: Rains fuel dengue surge: Pune city records 560 suspected cases, 212 in July alone
article.articleSummary: Dengue surge in Pune, India, fueled by monsoon, with Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) reporting 560 suspected cases, including 212 in July—the highest total. National Institute of Virology confirms 22 dengue cases; seven chikungunya cases also recorded, with no significant chikungunya outbreak this year. Case counts show a monsoon-driven rise: 58 in May, 175 in June, 212 in July. PMC classifies cases as suspected when NS-1 antigen tests are positive; only ELISA IgM or IgG positivity yields confirmed status. Intensified vector-control includes surveillance in residential societies, offices, schools, and other sites, leading to 1,184 mosquito-breeding spots eliminated and 1,184 notices issued; penalties recovered amount to ₹14.31 lakh. Clinicians report classic dengue symptoms—high fever and low platelets—with no severe cases so far; treatment remains supportive, and there are no proven antivirals. Authorities warn of rises in 10–15 days due to continued rainfall; residents urged to eliminate stagnant water and seek care.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "Dizziness and fatigue are the first symptoms of a new COVID variant because the virus attacks the intestines? - Check the Facts."
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 misinformation check: dizziness and fatigue are not proven as early, variant-specific symptoms, and there is no evidence that a new strain starts by attacking the intestinal lining. Dizziness can have many causes and is not a diagnostic sign of infection or neural damage. Some COVID-19 patients may have gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea), but these are not established as common initial features of a new variant. Long COVID—prolonged fatigue in some recovered patients—is acknowledged by WHO but does not affect all cases. Claims that eggs or milk intake prevents or mitigates COVID-19 lack scientific support. In Thailand, the dominant circulating lineage is JN.1; from Jan 1 to July 19, 2026, there were 27,333 cases and 3 deaths, mostly among the elderly, with a healthcare system able to cope. Public health measures include DMH: frequent handwashing, masking in crowded places, and ATK testing when symptomatic.

triage.headline_ja: 「めまい・疲労感」は新型コロナ変異株の初期症状で腸を攻撃するせい？：ファクトチェック

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lakhimpur: During the monsoon season, the risk of Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) in animals is higher; get a free vaccination.
article.articleSummary: During the monsoon in Lakhimpur Kheri district, Uttar Pradesh, Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) poses a major risk to cattle, buffalo, goats, and other dairy animals, reducing milk production and causing economic losses. Animals develop mouth ulcers, excessive saliva, fever, and hoof lesions leading to lameness if untreated. To curb the outbreak, the veterinary department has launched a free, door-to-door FMD vaccination campaign. Chief Veterinary Officer Dr. Dinesh Sachan says special teams will visit villages and homes across the district, with no need for farmers to go to clinics. The free vaccination runs until September 8. Farmers are advised to keep animals' housing clean and dry, avoid standing dirty water, and contact nearest veterinary center if symptoms appear. The campaign aims to protect livelihoods and livestock during the monsoon season.

article.articleHeadline: Sốt rét ác tính gây suy đa cơ quan: Cảnh báo và điều trị hiệu quả năm 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Severe malaria causing multi-organ failure: Warning and effective treatment in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Two patients with severe falciparum malaria were discharged from Bach Mai Hospital in Hanoi, Vietnam, by 25 July 2026 after recovering from life-threatening multi-organ failure. The Vietnamese man, 51, and a Chinese national, 38, presented in critical condition with altered consciousness and multi-organ injury; the Chinese patient required mechanical ventilation and continuous renal replacement therapy. Treatment was hampered by a shortage of injectable artesunate, but with support from the Ministry of Health and the World Health Organization, artesunate was promptly coordinated to Vietnam, aiding parasite clearance and patient survival. The report underscores that severe malaria can progress rapidly, affecting brain, liver, kidneys, lungs, and other organs. WHO notes malaria is well controlled in Vietnam, but imported cases from endemic regions occur; travelers returning from such areas should seek prompt evaluation for fever, chills, headache or fatigue to prevent progression to severe malaria.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The world's first Bundibugyo-type Ebola vaccine begins human trials.
article.articleSummary: As of July 25, 2026, the world’s first human trial of a Bundibugyo ebolavirus vaccine has begun. Oxford University’s Vaccine Group and the Pandemic Sciences Institute administered the first dose of the ChAdOx1 BDBV candidate vaccine in a historic Phase 1 study, with ongoing recruitment to assess safety and immune responses. The project is CEPI-funded, and researchers plan further clinical testing in Uganda pending regulatory approval. Context notes that Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Kinshasa) and Uganda were declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern by the WHO on May 17, 2026, and there are no approved vaccines or therapies for Bundibugyo ebolavirus yet.

article.articleHeadline: Kontak Erat Pasien TB Dapat Terapi Pencegahan, Ini Alasannya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Close Contacts of TB Patients Eligible for Preventive Therapy, Here's Why.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia launches expanded tuberculosis screening with free chest X-ray checks at 53,335 locations nationwide to rapidly identify and treat suspected TB cases. Close contacts of TB patients who show no symptoms will receive Tuberculosis Preventive Therapy (TPT) to prevent progression to active disease. Deputy Health Minister Dr. Benjamin Octavianus, nicknamed Benny, announced in Jember on 24 July 2026 that TB bacteria can reside in the body for 1–2 years before disease develops, highlighting the importance of early preventive therapy to interrupt transmission. Indonesia remains the second-highest TB burden globally, behind India and above China. The ministry backs the Homecare program, in which health workers visit households for basic health checks, provide education, and, when needed, use telemedicine for doctor consultations. Authorities call on local governments to support CKG chest X-ray screening and ensure community participation to find and treat TB earlier.

article.articleHeadline: Benguet town suspends school uniform rule as dengue cases rise
article.articleSummary: La Trinidad, Benguet—Mayor Roderick Awingan issued Executive Order No. 102, Series of 2026, suspending the mandatory wearing of standard public school uniforms for one month to curb dengue infections amid rising local cases. The order formalizes the DOH’s 4S dengue prevention strategy (Search and destroy breeding sites, Self-protection, Seek early medical care, and Avoid indiscriminate fogging) and directs all barangays and public and private schools to intensify vector-control efforts. Officials reported 95 dengue cases in La Trinidad from January–July 2026, underscoring ongoing risk to schoolchildren. Students should wear long-sleeved shirts, full-length pants, high socks and closed shoes; enrollment is not denied for non-uniform attire if clothing is clean and appropriate. Weekly 'Search and Destroy' drives, sanitation inspections, and Aksyon Barangay/Paaralan Kontra Dengue are mandated, with MDRRMO, DOH oversight, and funding from LDRRM and local health allocations. In effect immediately for one month unless extended.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue could pose a danger to diabetic patients! Why is this mosquito deadly for Type-2 diabetics? Find out from a doctor.
article.articleSummary: Dengue could be more dangerous for people with Type-2 diabetes, according to a review in the International Journal of Diabetes & Technology. In dengue-prone areas, diabetics should receive regular care and consider dengue vaccination. High blood sugar weakens immunity, speeding dengue virus spread and raising risks of platelet drops, internal bleeding, and Dengue Shock Syndrome. Risk is higher with age, obesity, kidney disease, and poor glycemic control. In India, over 100 million people have diabetes, with heart attack, stroke and severe infections 2–4 times more likely than in non-diabetics. Early dengue symptoms in diabetics resemble others: fever, body and joint pain, headache, retro-orbital pain, nausea, vomiting, and rashes; warning signs include persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain and bleeding. Prevention includes repellents, long sleeves, removing standing water, controlling blood sugar, hydration, and a balanced diet. If dengue occurs, practitioners at KIMS Hospital, Thane, may temporarily adjust diabetes medications with close monitoring.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Suminwa visits the Ituri outbreak hotspots as the epidemic surpasses 1,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri region has surpassed 1,000 deaths. As of July 21, 2,536 laboratory-confirmed cases were reported with 1,033 deaths and 506 recoveries (case fatality 40.7%), with Ituri accounting for about nine of ten cases. article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola virus is gaining ground.
article.articleSummary: In eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak is expanding on two fronts, the viral epidemic and armed conflict, per United Nations remarks. Over weeks, the outbreak has grown in provinces long ravaged by fighting, with insecurity and population displacement complicating the response. Attacks on treatment centers by armed groups have hindered containment. Since the outbreak’s official declaration on May 15, the seventeenth Ebola outbreak in DRC, the number of confirmed cases reached 2,473 across five provinces: Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo as of July 20. The World Health Organization reports the death toll exceeding 1,000. The conflict has reached facilities and impeded the fight against Ebola, underscoring the two-pronged challenge: ongoing transmission and insecurity in the affected regions.

article.articleHeadline: सतर्कता: भारत और क्यूडेंगा डेंगू वैक्सीन
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Caution: India and the Qdenga Dengue Vaccine.
article.articleSummary: India’s CDSCO approved Takeda’s Qdenga; this marks India’s first dengue vaccine approval after WHO prequalification and licenses in 40+ countries. The decision follows dengue’s worst years and surveillance, with Aedes mosquitoes now spreading into semi-urban and rural areas where control is harder. Qdenga is designed to be given regardless of prior dengue infection, unlike Dengvaxia, but must confer protection against all four serotypes. Data show protection against DEN‑2 and DEN‑1, with uncertainty for DEN‑3 and DEN‑4 in seronegative individuals. This matters since DEN‑2 is common in India while DEN‑3 is rising; a DEN‑3 surge during the monsoon could blunt impact, especially for those with no prior dengue. The two-dose schedule (three months apart) may complicate uptake among migrant workers and children who miss vaccination. Price variability could make Qdenga costly in urban slums; price negotiations are essential to reach high-risk populations. Deployment remains challenging and should not replace vector control.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Jinjiang CDC reminds residents to watch for a summer COVID-19 'small peak'
article.articleSummary: Jinjiang City Center for Disease Control and Prevention warns residents of a summer uptick in COVID-19 cases. Local reports show more fever and sore throat, with some residents testing positive for SARS-CoV-2. National sentinel data indicate rising influenza-like illness positivity, but overall circulation remains low. The summer “small peak” is linked to indoor air conditioning with limited ventilation, dry mucosa, and increased travel and gatherings. Most infections are mild, resembling a cold or flu, and resolve in about a week. High‑risk groups—older adults, those with hypertension or diabetes, and the immunocompromised—should seek care if fever persists, chest tightness, or fatigue, and wear a mask during medical visits. Preventive measures include regular ventilation (open windows for 10–15 minutes every 2–3 hours), open windows during cooler periods, a light diet, regular sleep, and masking in crowded indoor spaces such as cinemas, malls, and stations.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Warning: Risk of infectious disease transmission to humans from ticks and mites on pets.
article.articleSummary: Hue, Vietnam – MB Vet Hue reports over 30 dogs treated for blood parasites transmitted by ticks and mites in the past two weeks, signaling a serious zoonotic risk. Babesia and Ehrlichia cause fever, nosebleeds, and can be fatal without timely care; tick bites can also transmit disease to humans, including fever, rash, or Lyme-like joint pain. Beyond pets, parasites carried by dogs and cats threaten people. Toxocara eggs on fur or floors can cause visceral larva migrans, affecting liver, lungs, eyes, or brain; Ancylostoma (hookworm) larvae penetrate the skin, causing itch and anemia. Echinococcus tapeworms can form cysts in liver and lungs, sometimes requiring surgery. Preventive measures: deworming puppies every 2 weeks to 3 months, then monthly to 6 months; dogs then every 3 months; humans every 6 months. Practice good hygiene, clean daily, avoid raw meat, and seek medical tests for persistent itching or hives.

article.articleHeadline: Surto de ebola com propagação mais rápida da história testa resposta de saúde global
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak with the fastest spread in history tests the global health response.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) represents the fastest-spreading on record. By July 25, 2026, the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain has caused 2,473 confirmed cases and 999 deaths in the DRC, with Uganda reporting two deaths, for a total of 1,001 fatalities. The Ituri Province, particularly Bunia, is the epicenter, accounting for more than 90% of cases and about 80% of deaths. Over 100 infections among health workers, including at least 36 fatalities, have been reported. No licensed vaccines or targeted treatments exist for Bundibugyo; vaccines like Ervebo and monoclonal antibody therapies for Zaire are not effective. The disease often begins with flu-like symptoms, delaying diagnosis and isolation. About 80% of new cases are outside known contact lists; models suggest true scale could be 2-4 times higher. Conflict, displacement, and cross-border movement complicate response; risks to neighboring countries including Burundi and Ethiopia.

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo: More people seeking treatment for Ebola as trust grows
article.articleSummary: As of 25 July 2026, Bunia in Ituri province, DR Congo, remains the epicentre of the current Ebola outbreak. More than 2,500 cases have been reported, with over 1,000 deaths since mid-May, most occurring in communities rather than treatment centres. Growing trust is drawing more people to about a dozen Ebola Treatment Centres, including the Evangelical Medical Centre in Bunia, though at least 12 facilities have been attacked due to fear and misinformation. Ongoing insecurity and conflict limit access, suggesting the true burden could be more than twice the reported figure. Contact tracing reaches around 80% of identified contacts, but many communities remain unreachable, and diagnoses and rapid deployment are incomplete. Priorities include reducing transmission in Ituri via enhanced surveillance, safe burials, clinical management, and community engagement, plus rapid capacity building in newly affected provinces. WHO cites technical challenges and calls for ceasefire and sustained international support.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever nationwide tops 100 cases; construction sites have the highest positivity rate for disease-carrying mosquitoes; Tainan strengthens patrols to seal gaps.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever in Taiwan reaches 100 cases this year as of July 24: 7 locally transmitted and 93 imported, with infections mainly linked to Indonesia, Vietnam, the Maldives, and Malaysia. El Niño-driven heat and rainfall shifts raise vector breeding risk amid the summer travel surge. Tainan City convened the 2026 second anti-epidemic meeting to marshal central, local, and private resources, strengthening surveillance, preparedness, and community involvement. From January–June, Tainan’s Dengue Prevention Center captured over 370,000 Aedes eggs, conducted 630 mobilization actions, inspected 35,398 households, found 4,150 standing-water containers, and educated 21,089 people. High-risk sites (6,877 inspections) yielded 185 positive containers; construction sites 5.52% positive, parks 4.72%, tourist attractions 4.70%. Recommendations include dedicated inspections for recurrent breeding sites, reinforced hospital environmental management, and Japanese encephalitis vaccination for high-risk workers; NS1 rapid tests for early dengue diagnosis are used. Ongoing COVID-19, flu vaccination campaigns, and weekly “patrol, drain, clean, scrub” remain emphasized, with underground construction highlighted as a potential breeding source.

article.articleHeadline: Evropou se šíří kapavka: Antibiotika přestávají zabírat!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gonorrhea Spreading Across Europe: Antibiotics Are No Longer Working.
article.articleSummary: Gonorrhea resistant to antibiotics is spreading across Europe, with local transmission now evident beyond travel-related cases. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) warns Neisseria gonorrhoeae is increasingly resistant to ceftriaxone, and often to azithromycin, undermining standard dual therapy. The largest increases are reported in the United Kingdom, France, Germany and Sweden, though several other countries report isolated cases; the situation could accelerate during the summer travel season. Previously travel-associated, resistant strains are now circulating among residents. Southeast Asia remains the main source region for imported strains, with high-risk destinations including Thailand, Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam for travelers with new sexual contacts. Over the last decade, European gonorrhea cases rose about 303%; in 2024 Europe logged over 106,000 confirmed cases—the highest since monitoring began in 2009. Untreated gonorrhea can cause pelvic inflammatory disease, ectopic pregnancy, or infertility.

The EBO-PEP trial began July 14 in the DRC and Uganda to evaluate post-exposure prophylaxis with obeldesivir.

article.articleHeadline: How Typhoid Spreads: 7 Everyday Mistakes That Increase Your Infection Risk
article.articleSummary: Typhoid fever, caused by Salmonella Typhi, affects millions annually and spreads mainly through contaminated water or food in regions with unsafe sanitation. Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, announced a typhoid diagnosis and ongoing treatment, highlighting the personal impact. The article lists seven everyday mistakes that raise risk: drinking unsafe water; eating food prepared in unhygienic conditions; skipping handwashing; consuming raw fruits and vegetables washed with contaminated water; ignoring home food hygiene; assuming vaccination or a clean environment alone suffices; delaying care for persistent fever. Prevention emphasizes drinking boiled or filtered water, frequent handwashing with soap, freshly cooked meals, washing or peeling produce, vaccination where recommended, and prompt medical evaluation for fever. Typhoid often presents with sustained high fever, weakness, headache, abdominal pain, and digestive symptoms; diagnosis and antibiotics are essential.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola thrives in DR Congo's chaos. The world may soon pay the price
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) escalates amid protracted conflicts in the east, with more than 1,000 confirmed deaths and over 2,500 infections; the virus has spread to neighboring Uganda. The security crisis has fragmented control, limiting access to affected communities, disrupting surveillance and vaccination, and fueling mistrust of responders. Cross-border transmission elevates the risk of imported cases to other countries, including the United States, sustaining a global vigilance and potential economic instability in the region. Health authorities and UN peacekeepers struggle to keep pace as armed groups, such as M23, ADF, and CODECO, shift alliances and contest territories in North and South Kivu and Ituri, creating a dangerous blind spot for containment. As of 2026-07-25, containment remains challenging, and the outbreak threatens broader regional stability.

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en República Democrática del Congo supera los 1.300 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 1,300 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 1,300 deaths (case fatality 44%) as of July 23, with 766 patients in isolation or hospitalized and 540 recoveries; contact tracing stands at 73.9%. Five provinces are affected: Ituri (epicenter), North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. The INSP cautions that surveillance must be reinforced due to ongoing transmission and data delays. Declared May 15 in Ituri, the outbreak spread to Uganda, which reported 20 cases (15 imported from the DRC) and 2 deaths; Uganda began a 42-day countdown after the last hospitalized patient was discharged on July 16. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus; there is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment, with WHO assigning high risk in sub-Saharan Africa and low global risk. Transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and bleeding. This is the third-worst Ebola epidemic and 17th outbreak in the DRC.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in Congo is out of control.
article.articleSummary: As of July 25, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 1,000 deaths and about 2,500 confirmed cases, marking the fastest-spreading outbreak to date for the Bundibugyo Ebola virus. The World Health Organization reports five eastern provinces affected: Ituri (accounting for more than 90% of cases and 80% of deaths), North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. Ongoing insecurity hampers response, with teams focusing on Bunia and surrounding areas. Strategic adjustments aim to tailor interventions per region. Encouraging signs emerged in Mongbalo, where the outbreak was first detected, with similar stabilization trends in Goma, North Kivu. The Bundibugyo virus is highly infectious and, in past outbreaks, caused fatality rates up to about 40%; there is no vaccine or approved treatment for this strain.

The operation is part of immediate containment and control to reduce further virus transmission within the affected area and neighboring communities. The CVO urged hog raisers to heighten biosecurity and report any unusual illness or mortality. The ASF Task Force has been reactivated, and the city prohibits entry of all live pigs, pork, and pork products from areas with confirmed ASF cases.

article.articleHeadline: É possível pegar dois vírus ao mesmo tempo: entenda como acontecem as coinfecções respiratórias
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Is it possible to contract two viruses at the same time? Understand how respiratory coinfections occur.
article.articleSummary: Coinfections with multiple respiratory viruses are possible, especially during the winter, when simultaneous circulation of influenza, RSV, rhinovirus, and SARS-CoV-2 occurs in Brazil. The Fiocruz InfoGripe bulletin notes over 100,000 severe acute respiratory illness (SARI) cases in 2026 with co-circulation of RSV, rhinovirus, influenza A, influenza B, and SARS-CoV-2. Symptoms often overlap (fever, cough, congestion, sore throat, malaise), making clinical distinction difficult. Molecular multiplex respiratory panels using real-time PCR can detect numerous viruses and bacteria from a single sample in about one hour, enabling identification of coinfections and guiding clinical decisions. High-risk groups: children under five, the elderly, and immunocompromised patients. Accurate diagnosis can reduce unnecessary antibiotic use, addressing antimicrobial resistance emphasized by WHO. Overall, multiplex testing enhances diagnostic precision and supports timely, evidence-based care for patients with respiratory infections in Brazil.

article.articleHeadline: COVID-19 Cases Rise In Telangana And Andhra Pradesh, Health Officials Say No Need to Panic
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 cases rise in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, but officials say there is no cause for panic. In Telangana, Dr. B. Ravinder Nayak said the uptick is a mild seasonal trend with no evidence of increased severity or any new Variant of Concern, and surveillance is ongoing with the Union government. Elderly and those with underlying health conditions are advised to follow basic precautions and avoid crowded, poorly ventilated places. The Union Ministry cites IDSP, ICMR, CMC Vellore, and other experts as not indicating countrywide concern. In Andhra Pradesh, three new cases have been reported in East Godavari and Visakhapatnam, raising active cases to 32 with four deaths in the state. Measures include enhanced testing and treatment, availability of testing kits, medicines, PPE, and dedicated COVID-19 beds. A total of 255 dedicated beds across 17 teaching hospitals are kept ready, with isolation beds in secondary hospitals to be earmarked.

triage.headline_ja: テランガナ州とアンドラプラデシュ州でCOVID-19症例が増加、保健当局はパニックの必要なしとコメント
triage.triage_reason: 季節的な軽度の増加であり、新規変異株や重症度上昇の証拠はなく、当局は全国的な懸念はないとしている。既存の対応体制内で管理可能。
triage.notes: 当局は季節性の軽微な増加と評価し、新変異株や重症度増加の証拠なしと明言。既存の医療体制内で対応中。

article.articleHeadline: Infection risk looms large as CJP protesters fall ill
article.articleSummary: Viral infections, dehydration, and injuries are rising among protesters at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi amid scorching heat, humidity, and overcrowding. Volunteer doctors report sore throats, headaches, high fever, nausea, and vomiting, with open-air living and inadequate food increasing transmission as infections spread via coughing and sneezing. By Wednesday evening, over 200 people had received paracetamol and related medications; many elderly protesters require medicines for diabetes and hypertension, with essential drugs supplied on-site. Injuries include sprained ankles from crowd movement and baton-related injuries during police action. Medical teams—four to five volunteers per shift from nearby medical colleges and groups such as Punjab's Five River Heart Association—provide paracetamol, ORS, antibiotics, wound care, chronic-disease meds, and cough syrups. The protest, organized by CJP, demands the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over a NEET paper leak.

triage.headline_ja: CJP抗議参加者らが体調不良、感染リスクが懸念される
triage.triage_reason: デモ参加者間での暑熱・過密による一般的なウイルス性感染症・脱水・怪我であり、病原体不明で公衆衛生上の深刻性や異常性、国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 本イベントは政治抗議（NEET試験リーク問題に関する教育相辞任要求デモ）に伴う集団感染様症状であり、感染症の病原体特定や公的な発生報告ではない。医療ボランティアによる対症療法（解熱剤、ORS、抗生物質等）で対応中。感染症危機というより群衆管理・熱中症対策の色合いが強い。

article.articleHeadline: Renewed Violence Fuels Deadlier Ebola Outbreak in Eastern Congo's North Kivu
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo’s North Kivu gains momentum as violence disrupts case finding and containment efforts. By 25 July 2026, fighting has driven more than 25,000 residents to flee into the northeastern city of Beni, complicating surveillance and access to affected communities. Armed assaults in the region have killed at least 60 people, underscoring security obstacles to outbreak response and vaccination or treatment campaigns. The article emphasizes that escalating violence is a critical driver of transmission risk, with limited ability to reach patients and implement isolation, contact tracing, and safe burials. The excerpt does not provide laboratory confirmation details, infection sources, or information on imported/exported cases, focusing instead on the public health and security context affecting the Ebola outbreak in North Kivu.

triage.headline_ja: 武力衝突再燃により東コンゴ北キブ州でエボラ流行が悪化
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の流行が武力紛争により対応困難となり、拡大リスクが高まっているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当しフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 武力紛争により症例探索・隔離・接触者追跡・安全な埋葬などの対応が阻害されており、感染拡大リスクが高い。25,000人以上が避難民となっており、地域的な人道危機とも連動している。

article.articleHeadline: Appeal for aid as DRC Ebola death toll reaches 1,000
article.articleSummary: Death toll in the Democratic Republic of Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 1,000 as of 25 July 2026—the 17th outbreak there in about 50 years and described as the fastest on record. Tearfund, a Christian development charity, appeals for additional aid to sustain life-saving interventions amid widespread ignorance and poverty that hinder prevention, and even attacks on some health workers. Basic hygiene is challenging where clean water is scarce. Tearfund’s response focuses on training faith leaders and community outreach to build trust, correct misinformation, and promote protective practices, while distributing chlorine, handwashing stations, and disinfecting churches. Local radio and online platforms (TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, WhatsApp) are used to counter misinformation. Donors, including the UK public, are thanked, but more support is urgently required to end the crisis.

triage.headline_ja: DRCのエボラ死者数が1000人に達し、支援を訴え
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で2項目（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性）に該当し、WPRO基準も複数該当。国際支援の必要性も明示されておりフルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 死者数1000人、過去約50年で17回目の流行かつ史上最速との報道。医療従事者への攻撃や誤情報の蔓延など、対応の困難さが強調されている。国際的拡大の明示的記載はないため不明とした。

article.articleHeadline: MS registra 9.686 casos confirmados de chikungunya - Agência de Noticias do Governo de Mato Grosso do Sul
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: MS records 9,686 confirmed Chikungunya cases - Government News Agency of Mato Grosso do Sul.
article.articleSummary: Mato Grosso do Sul (MS) reports 12,803 probable chikungunya cases in 2026, with 9,686 confirmed, per the 28th epidemiological week bulletin from SES on 23 July 2026. Chikungunya deaths reach 28 across Dourados, Bonito, Jardim, Fátima do Sul, Douradina, Guia Lopes da Laguna, Itaporã, Ponta Porã and Nioaque; one death is under investigation. There are 114 confirmed chikungunya cases in pregnant women. Dengue totals reach 4,718 probable cases, with 1,815 confirmed; no confirmed dengue deaths in 2026, and two deaths under investigation. In the last 14 days, several municipalities reported low incidence of confirmed dengue. Dengue vaccination: 241,030 doses received, 223,322 administered, 201,349 in the target population. The two-dose vaccine is given with a three-month interval and is recommended for children and adolescents 10–14 years 11 months 29 days. Public guidance: seek care for dengue or chikungunya symptoms, avoid self-medication, and eliminate water containers to reduce Aedes aegypti breeding.

triage.headline_ja: MS州、チクングニア熱の確定症例9,686件を記録 - マットグロッソ・ド・スル州政府ニュース通信

triage.notes: 記事はマットグロッソ・ド・スル州政府の定例疫学速報であり、ワクチン接種状況や公衆衛生対策も含まれる。ブラジルではチクングニア熱・デング熱は季節性・地域流行性の既知疾患であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限の兆候は見られない。

article.articleHeadline: Gripe, covid, sinusite ou alergia: o que os sintomas podem indicar - CSN1
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Flu, COVID-19, sinusitis or allergy: what the symptoms may indicate - CSN1.
article.articleSummary: During Brazil's winter, respiratory illnesses rise; authorities report over 82,000 Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) cases so far this period. Common symptoms—fever, cough, runny nose, and nasal congestion—can indicate influenza (flu), SARS-CoV-2 infection (COVID-19), sinusitis, or allergic rhinitis. Clinicians emphasize evaluating symptom progression and using laboratory tests to distinguish among conditions. Red-flag signs include shortness of breath, inability to perform daily activities, persistent fever, or worsening condition, with heightened vigilance for children, older adults, pregnant individuals, the immunocompromised, and those with chronic diseases. Diagnostic tools include molecular tests such as RT-PCR to detect influenza and SARS-CoV-2, and multiplex respiratory panels; blood tests (complete blood count, C-reactive protein) and total/specific IgE may aid assessment. Preventive measures include annual influenza vaccination, maintaining full COVID-19 vaccination, hand hygiene, and reducing transmission in enclosed spaces.

article.articleHeadline: João Gomes é internado com influenza e precisa cancelar dois shows
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: João Gomes is hospitalized with influenza and needs to cancel two shows.
article.articleSummary: Brazilian singer João Gomes, 24, was hospitalized overnight early Friday, July 24, 2026, at Real Hospital Português in central Recife after being diagnosed with influenza. Due to the viral illness, he canceled two upcoming performances: in Petrolina, Pernambuco on Friday and in Riachão do Jacuípe, Bahia on Saturday. He has since been discharged and is recovering at home. On social media, he shared a hospital bedside image; his wife Ary Mirelle posted supportive messages. In an Instagram statement, the artist's team said he will remain off work for four days, with rest, hydration, and temporary postponement of performances, rehearsals, and other in-person commitments. Return to activity will depend on significant clinical improvement, and only after at least 48 hours fever-free and a new medical evaluation. The aim is to minimize transmission to crew and public.

article.articleHeadline: Våld i norra Kongo-Kinshasa förvärrar ebolaspridningen
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Violence in northern Kongo-Kinshasa worsens the spread of Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak intensifies in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, outpacing Ituri's epicenter. Conflict-driven displacement and restricted aid in Beni have accelerated spread and raised mortality in the region. As of 2026-07-25, roughly 3,000 people have laboratory-confirmed Ebola infections in DRC. The article notes North Kivu's confirmed cases and deaths are higher than elsewhere in the country, linked to intensified fighting in Beni. The International Rescue Committee's Ebola group, led by Alice Ribes, warns that without prompt action North Kivu risks repeating Ituri's surge, including overwhelmed health responses and increased transmission due to population movement. The outbreak remains centered in North Kivu province, with Ituri still affected but not spreading as rapidly. No details on vaccines or specific infection sources beyond general conflict and displacement.

article.articleHeadline: Abhijeet Dipke diagnosed with Typhoid but fight will go on until Pradhan resigns
article.articleSummary: As of 25 July 2026, typhoid has been diagnosed in Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in New Delhi, India. The report provides no details on symptoms or laboratory confirmation. Dipke stated the illness will not derail the nationwide demonstrations demanding the resignation of Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, insisting the protests will continue until Pradhan steps down and any negotiations occur on neutral grounds. The movement is described as notable for peaceful participation, with Dipke thanking protesters across the country for their efforts. The article also notes Sonam Wangchuk ending a 26-day hunger strike; Dipke expressed relief for Wangchuk’s health but remained firm on the resignation demand. No additional infection sources, case counts beyond Dipke’s diagnosis, or imported/exported cases are mentioned.

article.articleHeadline: Veneno quebra resistência do parasita da esquistossomose
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Venom breaks the schistosome parasite's resistance.
article.articleSummary: Brazilian researchers from USP and Instituto Butantan tested venoms from eight Bothrops snakes (including jararaca and jararacussu) on Schistosoma mansoni, a major cause of schistosomiasis. In vitro, some venoms reduced worm locomotion, attachment, viability, and nearly abolished egg laying; Bothrops moojeni venom was the most impactful, with jararacussu venom notably reducing oviposition. Transcriptomic analysis of male and female worms revealed a systemic disruption in males (more genes affected, including those linked to cell division and neural signaling) versus females (alterations in reproduction-related genes). The study highlights noncoding RNAs as potential regulatory targets and suggests developing synthetic molecules to disable these RNAs as a new therapeutic approach. Currently, praziquantel remains the only available drug, raising concern about resistance given widespread use. Schistosomiasis affects about 200 million people, predominantly in Latin America and Sub-Saharan Africa; findings published in International Journal of Molecular Sciences (2026).

article.articleHeadline: More health workers strike as Ebola cases in Congo near 3,000, including over 1,300 deaths
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo's Ituri province, centered in Bunia, is the fastest-growing on record. Confirmed cases are 2,973 with 1,309 deaths; 766 patients remain in isolation or hospital and 540 have recovered, per government data. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, began May 15, and Ituri accounts for about 90% of cases. Health workers at the Elikya Ebola Treatment Center in Bunia went on strike over two months of unpaid performance bonuses, disrupting care, with Bunia General Hospital also affected by unpaid salaries. Authorities have yet to identify patient zero; displacement from conflict and mining movements hinder contact tracing. Response is hampered by a funding gap, attacks on centers, and mistrust. There are no approved vaccines or treatments for Bundibugyo virus, unlike Zaire virus; WHO says global risk outside Central Africa is low. A two-treatment study has begun in Ituri.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ感染者数が3000人に迫り死者1300人超、医療従事者のストライキがさらに拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRCイトゥリ州で史上最速の拡大を見せるエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行が継続し、致死率が高く、承認された治療薬・ワクチンがない上に資金不足と医療従事者ストライキで対応が妨げられているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョ株にはザイール株のような承認済みワクチン・治療薬がなく、紛争や鉱山労働者の移動により接触者追跡が困難。医療従事者への未払い問題によるストライキが対応をさらに悪化させている。WHOは中央アフリカ域外へのリスクは低いとしているが、域内拡大リスクは高いと評価。

article.articleHeadline: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke diagnosed with typhoid
article.articleSummary: On July 25, 2026, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced he has typhoid and is receiving intravenous treatment, but remains active in protests demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, who has resigned. The movement, led by CJP and centered at Jantar Mantar, focuses on irregularities in competitive exams, reforms in recruitment and entrance tests. Activist Sonam Wangchuk, who joined June 28, conducted a 26-day hunger strike; after the Centre gave written assurances—no cases against peaceful protesters, Parliament to discuss exam reform and accountability, and compensation for families of students who died by suicide following the alleged NEET paper leak—the fast ended. Dipke thanked supporters and said protests would continue. A separate item notes a constable's resignation on a CJP stage; Uttarakhand Police said the officer was already suspended.

article.articleHeadline: Congo-Kinshasa: Vaccin contre Ebola - Judith Suminwa rassure la population de l'Ituri
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo: Ebola vaccine - Judith Suminwa reassures the population of Ituri
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola response in Ituri centers on rapid field assurances as Prime Minister Judith Suminwa visits to assess the response on July 24, 2026. The visit to Ebola treatment centers in Rwampara, Bunia, and Mongwalu accompanies renewed government and partner commitments to eradicate the outbreak. Research led by INRB in Kinshasa aims to develop a specific treatment for the Bundibugyo Ebola strain and, ideally, a vaccine in coming months. The government has unlocked funds to begin patient care, with partners providing support; equipment, mobile laboratories, and vehicles are being delivered gradually, though some zones still lack mobile labs and health workers face payment delays. The PM highlighted broader health-sector concerns and the reinforcement of frontline staff. Efforts translate Kinshasa decisions into field action across Ituri as the outbreak response continues.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国:エボラワクチン - ジュディス・スミンワ首相がイトゥリ州住民に安心を呼びかけ

article.articleHeadline: সোয়াইন ফ্লুতে আক্রান্ত হয়ে আইসোলেশনে শাবানা আজমি! জানেন কেন হয় এই রোগ? রইল উপসর্গ থেকে নিরাময়ের উপায়
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Shabana Azmi in isolation after contracting swine flu! Do you know why this disease occurs? From symptoms to ways of recovery.
article.articleSummary: Indian veteran actress Shabana Azmi is in isolation after contracting swine flu (influenza A H1N1). Swine flu spreads rapidly between people via respiratory droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes, and can also spread by touching contaminated surfaces and then the face. Symptoms include fever with chills, cough, sore throat, body aches, headache, fatigue, shortness of breath, and sometimes rash. Diagnosis relies on flu testing, but results can take time, so isolation is advised if symptoms appear. Management emphasizes hydration, light meals, rest, avoiding crowds, and taking prescribed medicines. Azmi had planned to attend a protest meeting organized by a student group to support students but was advised by doctors not to go outside to prevent transmission. She posted on social media that she supports students and wishes for a speedy recovery.

article.articleHeadline: Amravati News: डेंगू के 56, चिकनगुनिया के मिले 26 मरीज, जुलाई में घटी रफ्तार, फिर भी खतरा बरकरार | 56 dengue cases, 26 chikungunya cases found, pace slowed in July, yet danger persists
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Amravati News: 56 dengue cases, 26 chikungunya cases found, pace slowed in July, yet danger persists.
article.articleSummary: In Amravati district, from June 1 to July 24, 2026, dengue cases reached 56 and chikungunya 26. July showed a slower transmission rate than June, but risk remains, with about one new dengue case daily among suspected samples. Rural areas registered more dengue than the Amravati Municipal Corporation area. July 1–24: rural samples (87) yielded 10 dengue and 7 chikungunya; municipal samples (46) yielded 3 dengue and 3 chikungunya. June figures: rural samples (373) had 35 dengue and 12 chikungunya; municipal samples (130) had 8 dengue and 4 chikungunya. Health department urges cleanliness and removal of standing water around homes to curb spread. The outbreak persists, with ongoing testing of suspected cases and continued vigilance in both rural and urban areas.

article.articleHeadline: Shabana Azmi tests positive for H1N1: Why shouldn't you dismiss swine flu as just another fever?
article.articleSummary: Shabana Azmi, 75, has tested positive for H1N1 (swine flu) in India, amid protests at Jantar Mantar. H1N1 is an influenza A virus that can cause pneumonia or respiratory failure and does not always present with fever. Common symptoms include muscle aches, chills, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, headaches, diarrhea and fatigue; emergency signs include shortness of breath, chest pain, dehydration, seizures, and severe muscle pain. High-risk groups are young children, the elderly, pregnant women, and people with chronic illnesses. Unlike many seasonal viruses, H1N1 can target deep lung tissue, rapidly progressing to viral pneumonia or acute respiratory distress syndrome, and in some cases triggering a cytokine storm with systemic inflammation. This raises risks of pulmonary embolism, DVT, and acute cardiovascular events. In 2009, the WHO declared a pandemic with about 284,400 deaths worldwide.

article.articleHeadline: Swine Flu Cases Surge: Common Symptoms Of H1N1 Virus To Look Out For And When To Seek Medical Help
article.articleSummary: Influenza A (H1N1) swine flu cases surge in Nagpur, India, with the year’s first death and about 25 cases since January. The illness is seasonal, not pandemic. Transmission is via respiratory droplets. Common symptoms include high fever or chills, persistent cough, sore throat, runny or blocked nose, headache, body and muscle aches, fatigue, sneezing; vomiting/diarrhea in children. Most recover within a week with rest and hydration, but some may develop severe complications. Seek medical care for difficulty breathing, chest pain, bluish lips, fever not improving, severe dizziness or confusion, persistent vomiting causing dehydration, or worsening symptoms after several days. High-risk groups: children, adults 65+, pregnant women, immunocompromised, and those with chronic conditions like diabetes, asthma, heart or kidney disease.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever on the rise, many residents of Dak Lak remain lax and complacent.
article.articleSummary: Dak Lak Province, Vietnam, is experiencing a dengue fever surge. From January to July 25, 2026, nearly 2,500 dengue cases have been reported across 102 communes and wards, about 10% higher than the same period last year. Outbreaks cluster in Ea Na, Ea Drang, Ea Súp, Phú Hòa 1, and Buôn Ma Thuột ward. The Tây Nguyên Regional General Hospital reports daily pediatric dengue admissions exceeding 40, roughly 15% higher than last year; most patients are 1–14 years old, with high fever, prolonged illness, seizures, or warning signs. Authorities urge vaccination for both children and adults, alongside aggressive vector control and environmental sanitation. article.articleSummary: In Goiânia, Goiás, Brazil, a dentist warns that during influenza, cold, or other viral infections, viruses and bacteria can linger on toothbrush bristles for some time, especially when stored in moist or enclosed spaces. The toothbrush itself does not cause respiratory illnesses, but can promote recontamination and prolong illness, with a cross-contamination risk to other household members. Choose soft or extra-soft bristles with uniform length and a rounded head; use a straight handle. Winter’s cold, dry air can heighten susceptibility to flu.

article.articleHeadline: Tes Mantoux TBC: Cara Deteksi Dini Tuberkulosis Lewat Kulit
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mantoux Tuberculin Skin Test: Early Detection of Tuberculosis Through the Skin
article.articleSummary: Mantoux tuberculin skin test (TST) uses intradermal injection of 0.1 ml purified protein derivative (PPD) into the forearm to detect prior exposure to Mycobacterium tuberculosis. In Indonesia, the world’s second-largest TB burden, TST is used for early detection and latent TB diagnosis. The procedure requires two visits; reading occurs 48–72 hours after injection. Induration thresholds: ≥5 mm is positive for HIV/AIDS, close contacts, and those with prior TB on X-ray; ≥10 mm for healthcare workers, diabetes or kidney failure, children under 4, and residents in high TB areas; ≥15 mm for those without known risk factors. Positive results do not prove active TB; follow-up with chest X-ray and sputum analysis is needed. Side effects are usually mild. Costs vary by setting: Rp30k-100k at government facilities, Rp100k-300k at private clinics; BPJS coverage is full with referral; IGRA costs Rp500k-1,000k and is less affected by BCG vaccination. If positive, further evaluation with X-ray and sputum is recommended.
